findings.scenario: A data engineer registers ImageNet-1k (1,281,167 train images) through the SDK. Each image needs POST /assets (logical_assets + assets rows), GET history, POST /upload (version_uploads row with a 24 h admission), the PUT, POST /upload/confirm (storage HEAD) and POST /versions (HEAD again). That is more than 6.4 M authenticated API calls, each opening a Cernere WebSocket, and about 5 M PostgreSQL rows before one training job can start. GET /assets/:id/versions is unpaginated and no batch or manifest endpoint exists, so there is no faster path.
findings.impact_ai_game: Datasets of 10^5-10^7 files are the normal unit of AI work (HF caps 10k entries per folder and 100k files per repo and still needs manifests). With a per-file aggregate, dataset ingestion is O(files) round trips against the shared identity service and the per-asset access predicate runs per row, so the catalog cannot act as the system of record for training data.
findings.current_state: One resource = one file; no manifest or collection object; search and list are per asset; Synergos has a per-project manifest.json but rewrites it whole on every file event (see AGD-AI-15).
findings.proposed_redesign: Add a `datasets` aggregate (kind: dataset | model | asset_set) whose content is an immutable manifest addressed by a BLAKE3 Merkle root: `manifests{hash PK, entry_count, total_bytes, parent_hash, created_by_principal, created_at}` plus packed, sorted entry files `manifest_entries{manifest_hash, path, content_hash, size, mode, chunk_map_ref?}` stored as range files (lakeFS metarange / Iceberg manifest-list pattern) rather than one row per path. API: `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/manifests` accepts an NDJSON manifest stream (path, digest, size); `POST /api/v1/uploads/batch` follows Git LFS batch semantics (server returns actions only for objects it does not already hold, <=1000 objects per page); `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/snapshots` pins a manifest hash as a named snapshot. Git commits only the manifest hash (DVC .dir / LFS pointer pattern); file-level history is derived by manifest diff.
alternatives: Keep per-file assets but add a bulk endpoint (fewer calls, same O(files) rows and permission checks)
Store each snapshot as one tar shard (simple, but loses per-file dedup and partial fetch)
Delegate datasets to lakeFS/DVC and link snapshot ids from Curare (fast, but breaks the single-catalog goal and the Synergos custody story)

findings.scenario: A curator approves a 2,400-image dataset as five submissions (<=500 each) and composes a release. POST /releases/:id/finalize calls resolveVersionClosure over the 2,400 selected versions; at the 1,000th visited node it throws acquisition_too_large (409) inside the transaction, so the release can never be finalized. Even a 900-file release that finalizes cannot be acquired if its dependency closure crosses 1,000 nodes, and acquisitionPlan then issues up to 1,000 presigned URLs in one Promise.all.
findings.impact_ai_game: Dataset snapshots routinely contain 10^4-10^6 entries and models ship with tokenizer/config/weight shards plus datasets; the release object, the only immutable approved set in the product, cannot represent them, so training reproducibility has no anchor.
findings.current_state: Fixed zod caps and an in-memory BFS over per-version rows (about 5 queries per node) with storage HEAD per node inside the lock; release snapshot is a JSON array of ids.
findings.proposed_redesign: Make submissions and releases reference manifest hashes (AGD-AI-01) so a 1 M-entry dataset is one row; compute closure as a recursive CTE over manifest_entries UNION version_dependencies with a server-side limit measured in bytes, not nodes; replace the bulk plan with a cursor-paginated `GET /releases/{id}/manifest?cursor=` that streams entries and a lazy per-entry or per-range capability endpoint; validate dependencies at finalize by manifest diff rather than per-version HEAD under FOR SHARE locks.
alternatives: Raise the constants (buys 10x, still O(n) HEAD calls inside a transaction)
Split datasets across many releases (breaks the one-immutable-set guarantee that training reproducibility needs)

findings.scenario: An ML engineer exports a dataset snapshot as 128 WebDataset tar shards (1 GB each) for the GPU cluster. Registering them with versioningType=reproducible returns 409; registering them as `working` makes 128 GB of regenerable bytes permanent and undeletable (AGD-AI-06); keeping them outside the platform loses the link between the shards and the source manifest, so nobody can prove which snapshot a model was trained on. The same applies to CLIP embeddings, thumbnails and BCn texture builds.
findings.impact_ai_game: ML pipelines are dominated by derived data (shards, embeddings, parquet previews, tokenized caches, converted textures). DVC's run cache and HF's refs/convert/parquet show the needed semantics: outputs keyed by hash(inputs, params, tool), evictable, and pinned when a release references them.
findings.current_state: The type exists only to be refused. Recipe/Run are listed as owned by production-pipeline but the only implementation is the single-row version_provenance table; thumbnails/CDN promised in G2 docs are absent.
findings.proposed_redesign: Implement reproducible as a cache tier: `recipes{recipe_hash PK = blake3(tool_id, tool_version, params_canonical, input_manifest_hash), tool, version, params, created_by_principal}` and `derived_artifacts{recipe_hash, output_manifest_hash, storage_class='cache', expires_at, last_access, pinned_by[] (release ids)}`; `POST /api/v1/recipes/{hash}/outputs` registers results; snapshot acquisition may request `format=webdataset|mds|parquet|thumbnail` and the server returns the cached derived manifest or enqueues a sandboxed job; a GC job evicts unpinned, expired derived artifacts from a separate reclaimable bucket/prefix (Delta vacuum semantics); finalizing a release pins the derived artifacts it references (HF side-ref pattern). Keep the rule that derived outputs never justify deleting a submitted source.
alternatives: Allow reproducible as a normal version with a TTL flag (simpler, but mixes regenerable bytes into the immutable version table and GC must special-case triggers)
Push derived data to an external DDC/lakeFS and store only the recipe hash (works if a DDC exists; loses release pinning)

findings.scenario: Publisher policy (Steam AI disclosure, EU AI Act Art. 50) requires a list of every shipped asset whose chain contains AI-generated media, with model identity. An asset went txt2img (model A, seed 42) -> upscale (model B) -> manual retopo in Blender. Curare can hold one provenance row for the final version: the two generation steps cannot both be recorded (PK is output_version_id; a second write returns provenance_already_recorded), `settings` has no schema so 'model' is spelled ten ways, and 'what was derived from source X' needs a sequential scan of a uuid[] column. The report cannot be produced reliably.
findings.impact_ai_game: Lineage model -> dataset -> code -> config is the core reproducibility and compliance artifact of AI work; OpenLineage and MLflow already define the vocabulary. c2pa-rs supports no glTF/FBX/USD, so the catalog must be the system of record for provenance of game assets.
findings.current_state: Single-row, forward-only provenance with JSON settings; cycle check and post-submission immutability exist; no run entity; domain_events are written but never consumed, so nothing can be emitted to a lineage store.
findings.proposed_redesign: Replace with a run graph: `provenance_runs{run_id uuid PK, job_namespace, job_name, tool, tool_version, environment{container_digest, code_commit, hardware}, principal_id, started_at, ended_at, state}`; `provenance_io{run_id, version_id | manifest_hash, direction in|out, role}` indexed on (version_id, direction); typed facets `generation_facets{run_id, digital_source_type (IPTC URI), model_id, model_weights_hash, prompt, negative_prompt, seed, sampler, params_hash}` and `quality_facets{run_id, assertion, success, column?}`. Queries: `GET /lineage/versions/{id}?direction=upstream|downstream&depth=` via recursive CTE; `GET /releases/{id}/ai-content-report` listing every entry whose upstream contains trainedAlgorithmicMedia. Emit OpenLineage RunEvents (datasetVersion = manifest hash, sourceCodeLocation = commit) from the outbox; for 2D/video formats Synergos embeds a C2PA manifest via c2pa-rs with hard binding = blob hash.
alternatives: Keep the single row but add a JSON schema for settings (cheap; still no multi-step runs or efficient reverse queries)
Store lineage only in MLflow/W&B and link by id (loses the release-time compliance export inside the catalog)

findings.scenario: An outsourcing vendor delivers 3,000 character illustrations under a contract that forbids machine-learning use. A year later the R&D team calls POST /acquisition/plan with the version ids (any `download` grantee can) and trains a style model. Nothing records the holder or the reservation, nothing stops the build, and the EU AI Act Art. 53 copyright policy or the JP Art. 30-4 'unreasonable prejudice' analysis cannot be performed because the purpose of the acquisition is never declared.
findings.impact_ai_game: Governance for AI training data is now a per-asset rights/consent bitmap plus provenance; CAWG defines the four entries, GPAI providers must publish training-content summaries, and storefronts require disclosure. Without the record the platform cannot be the system of record for AI governance in a studio.
findings.current_state: Assets carry name/properties/tags only; contract terms are deferred to later requirements; vendor sharing (Magic Link) is unimplemented.

findings.scenario: A scraped-web image dataset turns out to contain a person's ID card and an erasure request (GDPR Art. 17) or an AI Act Art. 10(5) deletion duty arrives. In Curare the version row cannot be deleted (trigger), the blob is excluded from reclaim because a version references it, and 'archive' only hides the asset. In Synergos the file stays in every peer's working tree (no tombstone propagation), every history node keeps all versions, offloaded copies sit in S3/GDrive in plaintext under the content hash, and embeddings/thumbnails derived from it are untracked. Conversely, a compromised Curare credential can call custody reclaim and unlink any object instantly with no grace period or hold.
findings.impact_ai_game: AI datasets are where consent withdrawal, opt-out and special-category deletion actually happen. 'Retain every version whole-file' must coexist with targeted, auditable erasure and legal hold; otherwise the platform cannot legally host training data, and a single reclaim credential can destroy a release.
findings.current_state: Immutability is absolute in Curare; Synergos has no delete semantics; custody delete has no brake. Org rule RULE.md §2 forbids DROP but expects logical deletion (`is_active = false`).
findings.proposed_redesign: Tombstone-based erasure with holds on both sides. Curare: columns `tombstoned_at, tombstone_reason, retain_until, legal_hold bool, retention_class` on asset_versions (trigger allows only these to change); `POST /api/v1/versions/{id}/erase` requires `manage` + step-up + reason, writes an `erasure_requests` audit row, keeps hash and metadata, marks derived artifacts (AGD-AI-03) and fingerprints for invalidation, and a purge job deletes the blob after the grace period unless legal_hold; `POST .../legal-hold` blocks purge and GC. Synergos: manifest format 2 with `{deleted: true, deleted_at}` entries and `FileOffer{deleted}` propagation; history nodes consume a Curare-signed purge list (hash, project, reason) and remove objects, sidecars and offloaded copies; offloaded objects are encrypted with a per-project KEK so crypto-shred works; custody `reclaim` gains a trash state with `retain_until` (S3 Object Lock governance-mode semantics) and requires a signed deletion intent referencing the operation.
alternatives: Keep absolute immutability and rely on crypto-shredding only (fails for derived artifacts and plaintext working trees)
Hard delete with no tombstone (breaks reproducibility proofs; manifests would dangle)

findings.scenario: A 40 GB bf16 checkpoint: on AWS S3 a single PUT is limited to 5 GB, so the MinIO-adapter path fails outright on S3-compatible clouds; the custody path caps a PUT at 1800 s (>=22 MB/s sustained) and a WAN drop restarts at byte 0; the client must first SHA-256 the 40 GB in one pass (the web client loads it into memory). Thirty fine-tune checkpoints of the same base are stored thirty times although 30-85 % of their bytes are shared; a GPU worker that needs one tensor downloads the whole file because no byte range can be requested or verified.
findings.impact_ai_game: Model artifacts (1-100 GB, iteratively edited) are the one workload where whole-file dedup provably yields 0 % and CDC yields 25-85 %; training loaders rely on 8-16 MB range reads of safetensors; without resume and ranges the platform cannot host model weights at all.
findings.current_state: Whole-file identity (BLAKE3/SHA-256) is sound, but transfer is single-stream whole-object on every path; the 2026-08-16 decision excluded CDC for all files; the chunker exists but is fixed-size and dormant.
findings.proposed_redesign: Add a size-tiered large-object policy (threshold e.g. >= 64 MiB or `kind=model|dataset_shard`): (1) keep whole-file BLAKE3 as identity; (2) store a Bao outboard tree per blob (~0.4 % at 16 KiB groups) so any byte range can be verified against the file hash and resumed; (3) for the tier compute a CDC chunk map with pinned Xet constants (GearHash, 64 KiB target, 8-128 KiB bounds, 64 MiB xorbs) and dedup chunks tenant-scoped; (4) uploads use IETF resumable-upload/tus headers with multipart parts >= max(10 MiB, size/10,000); (5) custody and MinIO GET honour `Range` with range-scoped signed capabilities (X-Xet-Signed-Range model); (6) receipts carry `digests[]` {sha256, blake3} plus chunk_count so clients hash once. Revisit the 2026-08-16 decision for this tier only, scored on HARNESS §3.5 axes: AI学習量 medium (Xet spec and xet-core exist), 作業コスト medium, 解決度 high, 主目的との一致度 high for AI assets.
alternatives: Server-side `zstd --patch-from=previous` for storage only (no differ, no client change; transfer stays whole-file)
Tensor-aware dedup (ZipLLM-style safetensors parsing) for higher ratios at the cost of format-specific code
Delegate model weights to HF Hub/Xet and only link (loses custody and on-prem goals)

findings.scenario: A PyTorch job on an 8-GPU node needs dataset snapshot S (120k images plus captions.jsonl). The only path is POST /acquisition/plan (<=1000 versions, 300 s URLs, N custody calls), after which the Node client downloads sequentially into `<uuid>.jpg`, so the relative paths inside captions.jsonl no longer resolve; every worker repeats the download because there is no shared cache or mount; URLs expire mid-clone and the refresh re-plans everything. WebDataset/MDS loaders, the S3 connector for PyTorch, lakeFS-mount or FSx lazy loading cannot be pointed at Curare at all.
findings.impact_ai_game: GPU time is the expensive resource; the industry pattern is an S3-compatible, range-readable, presigned surface over sharded sequential layouts plus a node-local NVMe cache. HF, lakeFS and Unreal Cloud DDC all expose one; per-file 300 s URLs are sized for artist clones, not epochs.
findings.current_state: Capability-per-file plans; names flattened by version id (spec forbids path rewriting); Synergos could fan out P2P but has neither range nor multi-source support.
findings.proposed_redesign: Expose each immutable snapshot/release through (a) a read-only S3-compatible gateway `s3://curare-{org}/{snapshot_hash}/{original/relative/path}` implemented as a thin ListObjectsV2 / GetObject(Range) / HeadObject facade over manifest_entries -> blob store, authorised by a scoped capability token (Biscuit attenuated to snapshot + expiry) instead of per-object URLs; (b) manifest entries that keep the original relative path (also fixes DCC cross-references); (c) `POST /datasets/{id}/exports{format: webdataset|mds|parquet, shard_bytes}` producing a reproducible derived artifact (AGD-AI-03) pinned by the release; (d) a Synergos 'cache node' role that serves ranges from the history store to the cluster with Bao-verified striping across history nodes; (e) documented loaders: s3-connector-for-pytorch, WebDataset, lakeFS-mount-style NFS loopback.
alternatives: Ship only a FUSE/ProjFS lazy mount (fragile across OS releases; tools that walk trees hydrate everything)

findings.scenario: Publishing a 1,000,000-file dataset through the daemon needs 977 PublishUpdate calls; each file bumps the manifest and rewrites the full pretty-printed JSON (about 150 MB at that size), i.e. roughly 10^14 bytes of writes and O(n^2) time; the receiving history node rewrites index.json per archived file; checkout fans out one FileWant gossip message per file through a 256-slot lossy broadcast; HistoryList/TagAdd responses exceed the 1 MiB IPC frame and the connection drops; conflict detection relies on CRC32, so a crafted collision is treated as 'unchanged'.
findings.impact_ai_game: Datasets of millions of small files are the normal AI unit (OFPA trees have the same shape in games); lakeFS, Dolt, Oxen and Iceberg all use Merkle or prolly-tree manifests so diffs and partial sync are O(changed subtrees). findings.scenario: A product reviewer asks which acceptance scenario proves that an ML engineer can pin a training set, trace a model to it and prove rights; none exists (UX-01..08 are artist/QC/release flows), so every finding above is out of scope by omission rather than by decision, and the data model keeps optimising for single-file artist saves.
findings.impact_ai_game: Without a persona and requirements, AGD-AI-01..18 have no acceptance criteria and no owner; the 'AI asset production' goal stated for the redesign is not represented in either repo's spec.
findings.current_state: Game-studio framing only; monetisation and UX docs do not mention datasets or models; Synergos uses 'AI' only in the decision-axis vocabulary.
findings.proposed_redesign: Add to spec/feature/ux-definition.md the personas 'MLエンジニア', 'データキュレーター' and 'コンプライアンス担当' with flows E (dataset snapshot -> training -> model registration with lineage), F (generated-asset ingest with provenance and rights) and G (erasure/opt-out request); add acceptance scenarios UX-09..UX-12 with measurable targets (entries per snapshot, time-to-first-batch on a GPU node, lineage query latency, erasure SLA); score the AI-specific design choices on the HARNESS §3.5 axes and register the spec set in Praeforma like the existing three documents.
alternatives: Declare AI data explicitly out of scope (then the 'AI asset production' goal must be dropped from the product thesis)
sources: maps/cu-docs.md §10 verbatim scan (re-verified by grep over spec/ and docs/)

coverage_notes: Read in full: all 11 available maps (sy-transport, sy-discovery, sy-content, sy-core-versioning, sy-history-hooks-ipc, sy-control-custody, cu-auth-access, cu-storage-transfer, cu-versioning-core, cu-workflow-infra, cu-docs) and the 4 research notes (ai-dev-data, vcs-game-ai, transfer-efficiency, breach-containment). The map sy-clients-docs.md was absent at start, after the other 11 maps, and on a further retry before code work; findings proceed without it, so Tauri GUI / Dioxus admin / ars-plugin client behaviour is covered only through the other maps. Every file:line in the evidence was opened and quoted from the working tree on 2026-10-15 (Curare HEAD b4b48dc per cu-workflow-infra map); where a claim rests on a map rather than my own read, the source names the map (AGD-AI-16 custody present(), AGD-AI-12 W24, AGD-AI-17 A10) and the sentence is phrased accordingly. Doc mentions of AI in both repos were scanned with ripgrep over spec/, docs/ and READMEs: Curare has none at product level (only developer-agent roles in docs/roadmap.md and 'Learn（学習）' in vision.md:38); Synergos has only the 4-axis decision vocabulary in docs/versioning-design.md:15. Not verified from primary sources (inherited from the research notes with their caveats): EU AI Act article text (community mirror), Japan Art. 30-4, S3 single-PUT 5 GB and 10,000-part limits, HF folder/repo limits, Xet dedup percentages; game-asset CDC ratios have no published measurement, so AGD-AI-07's tiering is scoped to model/dataset files only. Overlaps with other themes are intentional and cross-referenced rather than re-derived: the raw Synergos data-plane authorization hole (sy-core-versioning W-01) underlies AGD-AI-16; transfer mechanics (multipart, Range, CDC) underlie AGD-AI-07/08 but are framed here by the checkpoint and GPU-cluster workloads; deletion/legal hold (AGD-AI-06) and screening (AGD-AI-11) are governance controls that the security theme may also list from a breach-containment angle. Severity reflects impact on AI/game asset production fit, not exploitability. All 19 findings are design gaps or missing controls; none is an exploitable vulnerability in the narrow sense.
